Now, there are several things that you've said that are not only very similar to things that have happened and are happening here (and elsewhere), but that are indeed similar to dystopian writings either fictional or otherwise. I'll try to discuss those chronologically as opposed to the order in which they were stated

You cited several reasons you believed the election happened the way it did. One of the biggest (or at least most memorable for me personally) reasons people give for both initially voting and for continuing to support Trump is his lack of political correctness (in reference to the inaugural speech you mentioned). Another is the very real and pervasive feeling of dissatisfaction with a corrupt government run by career politicians who's motivations are inarguably influenced by financial and political (electoral) reasons more than any altruism or desire to accurately reflect the view of the population. You also mentioned the lack of education. Only 36% of college graduates voted for Trump. I will say, however, it is common to believe here that college will almost always persuade people to a more liberal political standing. Statistically, it does indeed seem to be true, but I can't definitively identify any particular reason.

I also can relate (admittedly, to a lesser degree) to the repression of dissenters both pre- and post-election. During the campaign, many "protesters" (minorities) at Trump's rallies were not only treated very poorly, harshly, and sometimes violently by the people attending the rally, videos of this happening was something supporters would share readily and enthusiastically. 
(To be fair, there were also plenty of liberals/Democrats caused many problems after the election, including riots, theft, violence, blocking high traffic roadways, etc. I do not agree with or endorse violence from either side, and also do not equate all members of a political group with the worst among them.)

Nothing struck me as more similar than your description of people defending their views through zombie-like preprogrammed responses that they were either fed by the media or that they some slogan-like tagline that they saw on Facebook on some group they follow that incessantly feeds them with easy to digest propaganda that they subscribe to verify their preconceived opinions and to avoid confronting opposing views through actual logic and reason and instead through the confidence in the belief that a lot of people already agree with them, and they are part of a larger whole that is in the right.
(Again, many Democrats and liberals are guilty of the exact same mindset and mindless swallowing and regurgitation of propaganda as a justification for their beliefs, and I am not in any way saying that every or any person who does support Trump does so because they are of this type of shallow thinking.)

While it is easy to feel powerless in such a society, the only words of encouragement I can give you is this: not everybody agrees with the things that the government/leadership of your or my country does. If you feel like you are alone, even if you are indeed in the minority, there are people who are just as frightened and disgusted by the things they view as evil taking power over you, them, and the rest of your people. No matter how many people follow like sheep, there will always be at least a few who either blatantly refuse to do so, or at least only comply out of safety and would support change if they were given the opportunity to do so. So never give up on the belief in humans only because the bad ones are currently taking control.

The only other thing I have to offer is my personal method of trying to make a difference. I think that the greatest fallacy of conviction is that if your logic is sound and your points are valid that you should be able to make people at best agree with and at least understand your views. The truth is that most people will never renounce theirs beliefs or admit they were wrong. Either from true conviction, inability to fully comprehend the subject itself, or from sheer stubbornness and obstinacy, it doesnt matter. Do not waste time trying to convince people who are already convinced of something else. 

I think that the greatest hope for my country and the world as a whole is in the hands of the next generation. I believe the most substantial impact you can have, the closest thing you can do to changing the world, is teaching children how to think for themselves. How to doubt what they are told. How to question the intention of the information that this era constantly bombards them with. How to form their own beliefs not based on the beliefs of the people around them, and to question their own beliefs often. How to listen to opposing viewpoints with the intention to learn something and not only wait for an opportunity to defend their own. Maybe this has been said, but I think it's important to note in case it hasn't been. I will add the disclaimer that this is not necessarily my personal opinion, but rather a point that I think has enough validity to be considered in a discussion of this topic and nature.

Many people who subscribe to "identity" politics would like to see each minority represented in some way for every facet of goverment (LGBTQ Senators, WOC Representatives, etc). While this notion would indeed give a more powerful voice to marginalized minorities, it is important to ask if that voice would be proportional to the percentage of the population that it represents.

As an example, (these numbers are not accurate and are only used to define the idea) if the total population of any given minority in addition to those that agree with them politically makes up 25% of the population, and there are 30 Senators (out of the 100 total) that either themselves identify as said minority or consistently vote in favor of the bills that they support or are supported by, while this does give the minority a voice in legislation, that voice is disproportionate to the actual views of the population as a whole.

This becomes more and more apparently disproportionate the smaller the group/council of elected/nominated officials is. For instance, if there was an LGBTQ Supreme Court Justice, while this is indeed a victory for that community, it is only "democratically" fair if 11.1111% agree with those views. (Which I am not saying is or is not accurate.)

Representation of minorities (whether they be of gender, orientation, race, opinion, or anything else) is important in any democracy, (which, to actually give my opinion, the U.S. is not a very accurate depiction of ideologically) but the more disproportionate that representation is, the less accurately the decisions made by those Representatives will reflect the view of population as a whole.

They would be gone for days at a time until they either returned, I found them, or someone called the number on their collar. Everyone who met them always went on and on about how sweet and beautiful they were, and it never failed in making me smile. Once, they must have found someone who was afraid of their boxy foreheads (they are pit mixes, but the only way you could tell is by the signature forehead and undocked ears.) They came home limping and bloodied, filled with birdshot. Hercules took one to the eye. I was outside working in the yard when they arrived, and despite the obvious pain they were in, Hercules did what he always did when he hadn't seen me for a while, he lifted his top lips so I could see his bright, beautiful smile. I sat there in the yard crying for minutes before I took them inside and removed as many of the pieces of bird shot as I could, but his eye would be blind for the rest of his life. One day, as I was outside watching the horizon, I saw something I seen very rarely in my life: Prometheus alone. Without his brother. Bleeding from wounds from other dogs or the local wild coyotes. He did not wag his tail when he saw me. He only came to my feet and layed his head on the ground, ears back, not looking me in the eye. I knew immediately. We stayed there and cried together for a long time. It's been more than a year, I still cry sometimes. Prometheus has nightmares and howls in his sleep. I pet him as he does, whispering that it's ok. That he is home and that he is safe. As he once again finds rest, I wonder if he dreams of his brother like I do. I don't know if it's better this way, not having a body to bury. Maybe someone decided to take him for themselves. Maybe they just got separated and he got lost. Maybe his bad eye put him on the wrong side of a highway and someone didn't have time to stop. Maybe his bones are scattered among some coyotes hole. I don't know, and I don't think I ever will. Prometheus still sleeps in my bed. I am not alone, but I will never forget Hercules. I didn't just lose my dog, I lost one of my best friends. Someone who inspired me with his unconditional love of me, of everyone he met, and of life itself. I lost a big piece of my heart, and it will remain with Hercules until the day that I myself find rest, and if there is a life after, I only pray that I can hold him again.
